drafted_from: tool row in tools/start-a-computer/tool-rows.json, do-work/start-a-computer.mjs (updateAComputer) and tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Update my computer a-computer to release new with my product settings and the signed release feed, keep a backup, and tell me the backup folder."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads the computer's own service unit and config over SSH and a request file, and writes the computer's settings, feed and release.
instructions: 1. Write request.json: ssh {known_hosts}, engine {file, release_name, release}, product_data (your settings manifest), release_feed {urls, public_keys, releases} (required), name {host_name}.

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:update-a-computer"} and runs node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs update lease.json request.json. No credential is needed; update one computer at a time.
3. Read the answer: layout, release, backup, product_settings, release_feed, copies and sign_up_status. Keep the backup folder it names.
4. To go back run node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs rollback lease.json request.json <backup>. A failed service or sign-up health restores the backup by itself.

worked_examples.ask: Update my computer to the new release and give me the backup.
worked_examples.given: From tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs ('an update reads a start-a-computer computer\'s own layout...'), run at 2026-11-04 17:15:00 UTC. The computer is laid out the way set-up-the-machine.sh makes it: unit place.service, state /var/lib/place, base /opt/place. request.json = {"product_data":"product-data.json","release_feed":{"urls":["https://releases.example.test/feed.json"],"public_keys":["aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"],"releases":{"keep":3}},"ssh":{"known_hosts":"/dev/null"},"name":{"host_name":"computer.example.com"},"engine":{"file":"trillion-local","release_name":"new","release":{"on_machine":"/opt/build/new"}}}. The feed has a release for the computer's target and https://computer.example.com/readyz answers 200. Run: node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs update lease.json request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"layout":{"unit":"place.service","config":"/var/lib/place/place.json","current":"/opt/place/current","state":"/var/lib/place","releases":"/opt/place/releases"},"release":"/opt/place/releases/new","backup":"/var/lib/place/backups/update-2026-11-04T17-15-00-000Z","product_settings":"/var/lib/place/product-settings.json","release_feed":{"urls":["https://releases.example.test/feed.json"],"releases":"/opt/place/releases"},"copies":{"least_copy_keepers":1,"least_voters":1,"least_may_answer":1,"least_always_on":0},"sign_up_status":200}: copies is 1 because the computer is alone; the backup holds the old place.json, unit and release pointer.
